subject: Cloud marketplace entry - SKU gating and co-sell criteria
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Maya Singh <aws-marketplace@amazon.com>, Azure Marketplace Team <azure-seller@microsoft.com>, GCP Partner Ops <partner-gcp@google.com>, L. Hart <linda.hart@enterpriseco.com>
Date: 2027-06-06T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Cloud marketplace entry - SKU gating and co-sell criteria

Team / partners,

Following up from our sync last week — attached is a first cut of the SKU surface we think makes sense for an initial multi-cloud listing and the co-sell criteria we want to propose to each marketplace. Key asks up front:

- Confirm which SKU granularity each cloud will accept (single large bundle vs. 3-tier: Starter / Scale / Enterprise).
- Confirm regional gating rules (we propose GA in US/EU, limited in APAC for launch).
- Clarify co-sell triggers (minimum ARR, POC completion, joint-marketing credits).

Attachments: sku_matrix_v1.xlsx (matrix by cloud/region/packaging), marketplace_entry_proposal.pdf (recommended timeline), co-sell_requirements_notes.txt (notes from partner ops).

Proposed quick decisions we need by EOD Tuesday so we can finalize the HubSpot opportunity and start legal redlines for AWS/Azure. High-level rationale below:

- AWS: Prioritize 3-tier packaging with an explicit ‘Dedicated’ SKU for enterprise customers using Dedicated/Private deployments. AWS requires clear product listing + seller-owned pricing for co-sell.
- Azure: They prefer a smaller set of SKU SKUs (one or two) to reduce listing complexity; recommend a consolidated Offer + metered plan.
- GCP: Good with multiple SKUs but needs a single VPC/private deployment offer for regulated customers (we can reuse Dedicated SKU naming).

Please reply with explicit "accept / modify / block" for each cloud row in the attached matrix. Maya, Azure and GCP reps — if there are hard constraints we should know now (minimum price floors, mandatory SKUs, regional restrictions), call them out.

Thanks—
Karthik
Director, Cloud GTM
Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: sku_matrix_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), marketplace_entry_proposal.pdf (PDF), co-sell_requirements_notes.txt (text)

From: Maya Singh <aws-marketplace@amazon.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Azure Marketplace Team <azure-seller@microsoft.com>, GCP Partner Ops <partner-gcp@google.com>, L. Hart <linda.hart@enterpriseco.com>
Date: 2027-06-06T13:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Cloud marketplace entry - SKU gating and co-sell criteria

Hi Karthik — thanks for the detailed doc and matrix. A few clarifications from AWS side: 

1) SKU granularity: AWS supports both multi-tier and single-bundle offers. For co-sell qualification we prefer a distinct enterprise SKU (or a meter) that maps to a subscription level so our field can track motions.

2) Regional gating: US/EU are fine. For any GovCloud or US-DoD-relevant SKU we need a separate listing and additional compliance evidence — call that out if you intend to sell there in launch.

3) Pricing floor: We have a recommended minimum list price for Marketplace transactions when the seller elects co-sell. I can share the exact ranges (by SKU) once I have the target ARR bands.

4) Docs + Legal: We can accept the proposed naming for the Dedicated SKU, but Seller-initiated terms (license/exclusions) must be attached as a supplementary document in the Offer. That typically delays approval by ~7 business days.

Note: On the co-sell triggers — AWS needs a named AE alignment + a minimum POC completion (demo + evaluation set) instead of pure ARR for initial joint motion. If you want, we can pilot with your EnterpriseCo prospect for co-sell qualification.

Best,
Maya Singh
AWS Marketplace Partner Development

Agree with Maya — two quick operational asks: 

- We should lock naming to avoid variance across clouds. Proposal: Starter / Scale / Enterprise + "Dedicated" suffix when applicable (e.g., Enterprise (Dedicated)).
- Ops-wise, create a canonical SKU -> Plan mapping in our internal marketplace registry (I added a tab in sku_matrix_v1). Ben / Soojin: can you take owning the registry and the HubSpot mapping?

One-line: AWS asks for enterprise SKU mapping + AE alignment; Azure likely wants 1-2 offers; GCP will accept multiple but expects a private deployment plan.

—Jonas
Head, Cloud GTM
Redwood Inference

Date: 2027-06-07T16:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Cloud marketplace entry - SKU gating and co-sell criteria

Thanks everyone — summary and action items below (please treat as decision record):

Summary decisions:
- Packaging: Agreed to three public SKUs (Starter / Scale / Enterprise). Dedicated variant will be the same name with "(Dedicated)" suffix for listings that require a VPC/private deployment.
- Regions: GA in US + EU for initial listing. APAC will be staged (Japan and Australia in phase 2). No GovCloud at launch.
- Co-sell triggers: Use AWS AE alignment + POC-completion (demo + eval run) as co-sell trigger for AWS; Azure to accept named opportunity + partner lead certification; GCP to accept AE alignment + legal ready status.

Action items (owners / due dates):
- Ben Carter: Create canonical SKU registry + map to HubSpot plans (due 2027-06-11).
- Jonas Weber: Draft naming convention doc and publish to Drive (done: see link).
- Karthik Iyer: Start legal redlines for AWS + Azure offers and share DocuSign with partners (due 2027-06-13).
- Maya Singh (AWS): Send recommended pricing floors for co-sell SKUs (ETA 2027-06-09).
- Azure / GCP reps: Confirm any mandatory listing constraints or additional compliance steps by 2027-06-09.

Linda (EnterpriseCo) — we included your prospective region (US) and the Dedicated SKU note. If you want us to pilot the co-sell process with your AE, reply and we'll loop sales engineering.

--
Soojin Lee
Director, Partnerships & Marketplaces
Redwood Inference
